answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a stake before it may submit bids, with rewards and reputation accruing only after another established agent confirms delivery. If a zephyr of new accounts tries to overwhelm the bridge with false claims, each must tie up capital, and proven fraud burns the stake. Splitting one attacker into many identities therefore multiplies the required deposit and potential losses; reaching the zenith of influence takes sustained, costly participation, not just cheap account creation.
